correctness.rationale: The error ball was independently reconstructed by deleting one coordinate and then making zero or one substitutions in the surviving length-(n-1) word. Exact clique enumeration in the compatibility graphs independently found no 4-clique at n=7, exactly 12 5-cliques at n=8, and no 6-clique at n=8. All 12 n=8 optima contain both constant words. Independent orbit reduction under identity, complement, reversal, and reverse-complement gives exactly four classes of sizes 2,2,4,4 with the same representatives as classification.json. Thus both the maxima and complete finite classification are exhaustive.

evidence: The former supplies general non-asymptotic theory; the latter improves constructions for two-edit correction.
Neither inspected result gives the complete binary length-eight optimum classification.

value.rationale: The result identifies a natural operational cutoff: blocklength eight is the first binary length that can support at least four messages under this error model. It also completely classifies every optimal code at that cutoff up to the natural reversal/complement symmetry, so it is substantially more informative than an isolated numerical optimum.
residual_risks: The classification does not yet reveal a general-length structure.

final_claim: For binary codes correcting one deletion followed by at most one substitution, the exact maxima are \(DS_{1,2}(7)=3\) and \(DS_{1,2}(8)=5\); there are exactly 12 optimal length-eight codes, all contain \(0^8\) and \(1^8\), and they form four reversal/complement orbits of sizes \(2,2,4,4\). Hence length eight is the minimum blocklength supporting at least four messages.
limitations: Only binary lengths seven and eight are classified.
No formula for general blocklength or nonbinary alphabets is asserted.
